summary.en: Turns the monthly AR bridge and overdue exports into a reconciled KPI scorecard, an AR bridge, cluster charts and a customer table — then generates the Excel master workbook, the PowerPoint deck and an email draft with both attached.

problem.en: Month-end receivables reporting meant rebuilding the same workbook and slide deck by hand from system exports: matching customers across periods and files, reconciling balances, and re-keying figures into tables and charts.

en: Reads .xlsx workbooks in the browser and finds the right columns by scoring header names, so changed headings or column order do not break it; the period is inferred from headers and sheet names.

Reconciliation checks: the AR roll-forward (beginning + sales + collections + offsets = ending), duplicate codes, customers missing from a period or from the overdue file, and low-confidence column matches.
KPI scorecard comparing the month with the same month last year, with the favourable or unfavourable direction stated for each measure.
AR bridge (waterfall) for the whole portfolio or any single customer, cluster charts for sales, collections, receivables and overdue amounts, and a searchable customer table.
Generates an Excel master workbook with formulas and native charts (11 sheets), a 12-slide PowerPoint deck with native charts, and an .eml email draft with both files attached.
Column mapping and cluster reclassification can be overridden in the page and are remembered in the browser.

summary.en: Prepares the export documents presented to a bank under a letter of credit — cover letter and bill of exchange — from a single entry, with the amount written out in words.

problem.en: Presenting export documents under a letter of credit means repeating the same LC number, invoice numbers and amount across several documents, and writing the amount out in words. The figures have to agree on every document before they go to the bank.

en: One form for the LC number, internal reference, customer, currency and one or more invoices; the amount is totalled from the invoices.
Cover letter to the bank listing the enclosed documents with original and copy counts, starting from an editable standard set.
Bill of exchange in first and second copies, with a supporting-invoice table.
Amount in words generated from the figure (for example “… and 50/100 US Dollars”), with a manual override.
A certificate of analysis generated from the same entry.
Live preview, and printing of one document or all of them.
A companion page in the toolkit prepares import-side letters: the LC request, comments before issuance and specimen-signature letters (not included in the demo).

notice.en: The original tool is used internally and contains organisation details, so it is not linked here. The demo is a separate rebuild for this portfolio with fictional names (Example Company, Demo Bank) and invented reference numbers. It covers the cover letter and bill of exchange.

summary.en: Writes a financial amount out in words in English and Arabic for 156 currencies — the wording used on cheques, bills of exchange and bank letters — with correct Arabic grammatical agreement and no rounding.

problem.en: Amounts in words must match the figures exactly. In Arabic the wording also changes with the number: the gender of the currency, the dual form for two, and the case of the counted noun all depend on the amount, which makes manual wording slow and error-prone.

en: English and Arabic wording side by side, with the “… and 50/100 … Only” and “… فقط لا غير” conventions.
Arabic rules for gender agreement, the dual, the counted noun after 3–10 and 11–99, and construct forms such as “ألفا ريال”.
156 currencies, including three-decimal currencies such as the Kuwaiti dinar, plus a custom currency definition.
Validation that rejects malformed amounts or extra decimals with a clear message instead of rounding them.
Accepts Arabic-Indic digits, inserts thousands separators while typing, and copies either wording with one click.
A built-in check suite of 154 cases covering formatting, grammar and error handling.

summary.en: Recomputes tiered commissions on letters of credit and letters of guarantee and compares the result with the amount a bank charged.

problem.en: Commissions on letters of credit and guarantees are tiered by amount and by period. Checking a charge on a bank advice means reproducing that arithmetic by hand.

en: Letters of credit: new issuance, increase in value, extension of validity, other amendments and advising.
Tiered opening commission on an L/C: a lower rate above a threshold amount, plus a monthly charge beyond the first three months.
Letters of guarantee: an annual rate pro-rated by days (Actual/365) or by months.
Optional bank minimum fee, VAT, and a variance check against the amount the bank charged.
A reference table of the rates used, which the tool attributes to SAMA’s Fees Guide for Financial Institutions’ Services, and a printable result.

notice.en: The original is an internal tool and is not linked here. The demo re-implements the same calculation for illustration only; its rates have not been checked against the current edition of the fees guide.
